title: Landmark hook
_note: An optional rumour/secret seed (appears ~half the time) — a light bridge toward the Hooks and small-oracle phases. Full sentences with their own terminal punctuation.

entries.value: Locals leave offerings at its foot and won't say why.
They say it marks where something lies buried.
Travellers use it to find their way for miles.
A rumour places a hidden cache somewhere near.
Something is said to nest within it.
Folk swear the dead walk here on certain nights.
An old road, now lost, once ran past it.
Those who camp beneath it report strange dreams.
A hermit is said to shelter somewhere in its shadow.
No bird will fly directly over it, the old folk say.
Coins pressed into its cracks are meant to buy a safe road.
Each spring someone wanders off near here and is never found.
A map in a dead man's pack marked this very spot.
Cattle that graze too close are found dead by morning.
They say a door opens in it once a year, at midwinter.
Two rival clans both claim it as their boundary.
A witch is rumoured to keep her hoard beneath it.
Compass needles spin wildly within a stone's throw of it.
Pilgrims still travel from far off to touch it.
The last person to sleep here woke a week older.
Local children are forbidden to go near it after dark.
Fresh diggings scar the ground where someone hunted for treasure.
An old song claims a king lies buried beneath it.
Herbs that grow nowhere else can be gathered at its foot.
Those who deface it are said to sicken within the year.
A caravan vanished near here a generation ago.
Something large is said to lair in the hollows below.
Storms are said to gather over it out of a clear sky.
Water drawn from its foot is prized as a cure.
A scholar in the nearest town will pay for a faithful rubbing of it.
Bandits are known to lie in wait behind it.
The bones of an old giant are supposedly sealed within.
Livestock will not pass it unless they are driven.
A hidden spring beside it never runs dry, even in drought.
Some swear it stands a little apart from where it once did.
The last band to camp here left in a hurry, gear and all.
Faint music is heard from it on the longest night.
Ravens gather here before any death in the valley.
A reward is offered to anyone who can read its markings.
On foggy nights a pale light drifts about it.
A wolf-pack dens close by and is seldom seen elsewhere.
An heirloom lost in flight from an old war is said to lie near.
